question.text: In a book built IPO, what does 'bidding at the cut-off price' mean for a retail investor?

answer.text: The investor agrees to accept whatever price is finally determined by the bidding process
The investor bids at the lowest price in the price band
The investor bids at the highest price in the price band
The investor is guaranteed allotment at a discounted price

explanation.text: The Logic: Bidding at the cut-off means the retail investor agrees to accept the final price discovered by the book-building process. Where the issue is oversubscribed, eligible applications at the cut-off are allotted on a proportionate basis as prescribed by SEBI. The Trap: Bidding at the cut-off does not mean bidding at the lowest or the highest end of the price band. It is also not a guarantee of allotment at a discount -- in oversubscribed issues, allotment is proportionate. Note: Workbook references: NISM Series XII pp.92, 95 and 98-99 support the definition of cut-off bidding and proportionate allotment in oversubscribed issues.
